title: Vibrant Light Stew Japanese Plum Jam Onigiri
description: A light and savory Japanese-inspired dish perfect for a sick day, featuring plum jam and a hint of tagine-spices, served as an onigiri in a terracotta dish.
instructions: Combine the Japanese short-grain rice and miso paste in a large bowl, mixing well.
Gradually add the miso-flavored water, stirring until the mixture forms a sticky dough.
Knead the dough for 5 minutes until it becomes pliable and smooth.
Cut the dough into 4 equal pieces.
Shape each piece into a ball and then flatten it slightly into a disk shape.
Place a small amount of plum jam in the center of each disk.
Add a few strips of shio kombu and some chopped aromatics on top of the jam.
Fold the dough over the filling, forming a triangle or a square shape, and press the edges together to seal the onigiri.
Heat a large tagine or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add a small amount of sesame seeds, if using, and then place the onigiri in the pot.
Cook for 10-12 minutes, turning the onigiri occasionally, until they are lightly browned and crispy on the outside.
Serve the onigiri hot in a terracotta dish, garnished with additional aromatics and a drizzle of soy sauce, if desired
